passage:
A new food label showed not only calories, but also sugar, salt, allergens, and origin.
A student with allergies said clear labels made her feel safer. Another student said too much information was confusing.
Their health teacher explained how to read the label step by step. Students compared snacks and were surprised by hidden sugar in drinks.
The label did not force anyone to choose differently, but it made choices more informed.
Food is personal, cultural, and emotional. It is also chemical and economic.
A small label connects the body to farms, factories, laws, and daily habits.
